name: Reassignment
summary: In Southshore, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle seeks a way back to Stormwind. He has compiled an exaggerated report of his deeds against the coastal naga and sends an adventurer to Stormwind Keep to deliver it to his former mentor, Major Samuelson.

sections.title: A Ticket Out of Southshore
sections.body: Lieutenant Farren Orinelle resents his posting in the Hillsbrad Foothills. In Southshore, far from the capital and under Marshal Redpath's stern watch, he spends his days plotting a transfer south. He takes credit for clearing out the nearby Daggerspine naga to make himself look like an indispensable, battle-hardened officer ready for promotion.

sections.title: Keep Connections
sections.body: Farren wants a transfer without drawing Marshal Redpath's suspicion, so he goes around the local chain of command. He turns to Major Samuelson, a senior officer in Stormwind Keep who mentored him in the past. A report delivered straight to Samuelson puts Farren's claimed deeds before someone with authority over garrison assignments.

sections.title: Bureaucracy at Work
sections.body: Major Samuelson receives the dossier in Stormwind Keep and gives mild approval to his former pupil's initiative against the naga menace. But military decisions move slowly. He promises only to weigh the report during next month's routine personnel review, leaving Farren's future in Southshore uncertain.

faq.q: Why does Farren Orinelle want a reassignment?
aliases: why does farren want to leave
faq.answer: Lieutenant Farren Orinelle wants to leave Southshore, a remote northern outpost he sees as dull, dangerous, and beneath him. He longs for Stormwind City's relative luxury and safety, and hopes his reports on the naga will justify a transfer.
Major Samuelson is a senior officer in Stormwind Keep who oversees city guard assignments. He mentored Lieutenant Farren Orinelle during Farren's early career in the capital.

faq.q: Why can't Farren deliver the report himself?
aliases: why do i have to deliver it
faq.answer: Farren is on active duty in Southshore and cannot leave his post without permission. He is also trying to bypass Marshal Redpath, his immediate superior, who would likely obstruct a transfer request made for Farren's own benefit.

faq.q: Did Farren actually defeat the naga himself?
faq.answer: No. Farren sent adventurers to kill Daggerspine naga along the Eastern Strand, then used their success in the report backing his request for reassignment.

faq.q: Does Farren actually get transferred back to Stormwind?
faq.answer: Not immediately. Major Samuelson promises only to consider the report at next month's personnel review. Farren remains stationed in Southshore for the foreseeable future as the kingdom's military bureaucracy turns slowly.
Major Samuelson is inside Stormwind Keep, the fortress at the heart of Stormwind City, where the high command and regency council reside.

angles.text: The delivery shows the everyday politics of the Alliance military, where frontier garrisons such as Southshore can be far from the ambitions of officers hoping to return to Stormwind.
The delivery shows the divide between human refugees and defenders holding the line in Lordaeron and the political maneuvering inside Stormwind Keep's high halls.
